content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm facing an issue with the [product_name] display. During simulation, everything works as expected, but when I upload the program to the device ([article_no]), the results are incorrect. I've configured the text message to show ON/OFF for a marker, and while it appears correctly in simulation, the device display does not reflect the marker status properly. Please review the program. Thanks.

Hello [user_name], I tested your program and it displays OFF first, then after triggering signal I1, it shows ON. I tested this with [product_name] [article_no], since downloading to [article_no] is not allowed.

Hi [user_name], I'm not sure why it's not working on [product_name] [article_no]. I have the 12/24 RC version. I'll check my application to see if the marker is ON. The operator sets parameters using the TD display, with the F1 key switching the parameter ON/OFF. While the program switches the marker, it doesn't update the display correctly. For example, changing the input parameter with F1 key (I1) works, but not with the marker.

Hello, [product_name] [article_no] only allows status text for DI and AQ, not for flags. This limitation was present in [product_name] [version_no]. Upgrading to [product_name] [version_no] resolves this, and when [article_no] hardware is selected, only supported options for status text are available.

Hi [user_name], I have a question—is it possible to assign any text to the counter on the TD display with [product_name] [article_no]? For example, I'd like the display to show a message to the operator indicating which program is being adjusted. Using a BCD pulse and a counter, I want the display to show descriptive text (like 'M14') instead of just numbers (e.g., 1 = Lietsse, 2 = M14, 3 = Din). Is it possible?
Hello, This can be done, but you'll need more than one counter. Please see the example attached. Regards,

Hi [user_name], This is a good suggestion, but it doesn't suit my application because I have two other parameters on the main screen. There are several combinations, with the screwdriver having three programs and the laser parameter being ON/OFF. I need the display to show which program is selected for the screwdriver and the status of the laser. I only want to change four characters on the second line, right side. I think it's not possible with [product_name]. Thank you.
Hello, In that case, you could create multiple screens with identical parameters except for the text you want to change. Regards,

Hi, regarding your initial question about status text: You want to use a digital flag to display a status text. As mentioned, [product_name] [article_no] doesn't support digital flags to trigger status text. If you have unused outputs on [product_name] [article_no], you can use one for the status text. There's an attached example showing how to achieve this with an unused output. Controlling an output on [product_name] that isn't wired or used is straightforward. Hope this helps.

Hi, thanks everyone for your responses. To [user_name]: I understand your suggestion, but the application has many combinations—this approach is challenging but not impossible. I'd prefer a simpler solution, because simplicity is best. To [user_name]: I don't have additional outputs; if I did, it would be easy. Thanks. I'll keep searching for a simple and effective solution.

analysis.insight_summary: Users struggled to show dynamic status information on the TD display using [product_name] [article_no] hardware. Simulation results did not match the physical device, mainly because the hardware cannot use internal markers (flags) for status texts—only inputs/outputs are supported. Several workarounds were suggested, but users found the limitations restrictive and solutions more complex than desired.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the TD display to provide real-time status messages that update according to internal program markers. They want hardware behavior to match simulation outcomes and ideally prefer straightforward solutions without complex logic or multiple screens.
